registered_before: The 136-game corpus is retrospective (weeks 1-9 were played before this file was written). The registration therefore binds the *procedure*, the *scored set*, the *benchmark*, the *holdout* and *every gate threshold*, and it forbids any post-hoc change to the model family. It is a registration of analysis, and it is labelled that way everywhere it appears. It is NOT a prospective registration and no prospective claim is made from it.
registration_hash_rule: The SHA-256 of this file is the registration. Adding a variant means adding a file, which changes the hash, which is a new registration.

corpus.why_week_1_is_excluded: A forecast for week 1 would have no prior week to learn from, so week 1 is excluded rather than forecast from nothing.
corpus.provenance: Final scores transcribed from NFL.com by-week schedule pages on 2026-11-14 and re-verified by this desk's own reconciliation against the same page text saved in nfl-results/evidence/.

holdout.rule: The scored weeks are divided by kickoff week, never by row. Weeks 2-5 are the development window; weeks 6-9 are the evaluation window. The split is fixed here, before any model in this desk is scored.
holdout.season_level_holdout_reason: This repository holds one season, so a season-level final holdout cannot exist. PG-SEASONS blocks any claim that it does.

model_family.rule: Seven estimators, each a stated function of prior weeks only. They are fixed in this file and in backtest.py; a build fails if the set or the parameter values change.

models.name: Null: league mean and home field
inputs: prior weeks' league points per team-game

models.name: Shrunk scoring profiles
inputs: prior weeks' points for and against per club

models.name: Pythagorean exponent
inputs: prior weeks' points for and against

models.name: Rest and bye differential
inputs: days since each club's last game

models.name: Home-only and road-only rates
inputs: prior weeks' home-only and road-only scoring

model_family.forecast_storage: Every forecast is stored as a probability and as a line, together with the inputs used: the league prior, each club's shrunk scoring rates, the rest days, and the source page of the result. See data/backtest.json.

benchmark.rule: Skill is measured against the same model with its club information removed, i.e. M00. A raw win rate is never used as a skill measure.
scores: Brier score on the directional probability
mean absolute error of the line
benchmark.cluster: Standard errors are clustered on the kickoff week, because games in a week share a league state.

gates.name: Probability stored
gates.rule: Every scored game carries a probability in [0,1] for side and total. A missing probability fails the gate.

gates.name: No leakage
gates.rule: A week-w forecast may use only weeks < w. The build re-derives every forecast from the prior-week window and fails on any other input.

gates.name: Benchmark-relative skill
gates.rule: Brier skill versus M00 must be positive.

gates.name: Cluster lower bound
gates.rule: The week-clustered 95% lower bound on Brier skill must exceed 0.

gates.name: Multiplicity
gates.rule: The number of variants tried is published and every p-value is BH-adjusted across that family.

gates.name: Holdout
gates.rule: The evaluation window (weeks 6-9) must not be used for any choice in this desk.

gates.name: Price
gates.rule: An entry may not be ranked or rewarded without an executable price. This gate cannot pass today.

gates.name: Prospective
gates.rule: An entry may not be called live without pre-kickoff recorded forecasts. This gate cannot pass today.

what_would_change_our_mind.toward_accepting_skill: A week-clustered lower bound on Brier skill above zero in the evaluation window, surviving BH over the full family, and reproduced on a prospective window with pre-kickoff timestamps.
what_would_change_our_mind.toward_rejecting_skill: A negative Brier skill versus M00 in the evaluation window, or a positive result that disappears when the development window is dropped, or a result that depends on one kickoff week.

forbidden: Changing a model parameter after seeing a score.
Publishing a backtest number in a leaderboard column reserved for a prospective record.
Reporting a win rate as a skill measure.
Using the evaluation window to select which model to show.
